newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds ended ahead on Tuesday, given a late lift as Bunds rose with U.S. Treasuries, but with cash business depressed by continuing EMU uncertainty, dealers said.
"The market was very quiet today and we were left to follow Bunds around, basically," one trader said.
With little retail buying taking place, business was concentrated in the 2003, 2004 and benchmark 2007 maturities, a broker said, but most trades were of fairly small size.
Spreads to Bunds remained stable at the long end, with guilders managing some outperformance in mid-curve.
"We were able to keep up with Bunds on their way up later on and that's a pretty good result," the trader said.

The market is expected to keep watching France and Germany this week as uncertainties about monetary union continue to circulate and cautious, range-bound trading is seen the likely pattern until new facts emerge.
Dutch fundamentals remain good however, analysts said, with the short-term cautious scenario brightening up in the medium term.
